intervals.label: approved / preparation
intervals.locator: no primary source consulted gives an exact CUPID approval or construction-start date
intervals.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) states CUPID's DOE Critical Decision stage or a construction-start date. A secondary web summary described CD-0 ('approval of mission need') and a prototype 'in construction' for mid-2025 data; that wording was not found in any primary source consulted, so it is not recorded. The collaboration's site (cupidexperiment.org/experiment/, checked 2026-10-25) describes the detector only in the future tense ('CUPID will profit of ...'). `start` (2025) is the year of the earliest dated CUPID collaboration paper found (arXiv:2503.02894, submitted March 2025), a lower bound and not a true approval or construction date, chosen so that an interval with no start does not derive to 'no presence'. That paper's Conclusions state 'CUPID construction activities have already started, including preparations for the cryostat upgrade and the setup of the detector assembly infrastructure' and that data taking is expected 'in the very early years of the next decade'; the status is nonetheless kept at `proposed` because the paper gives no construction-start date and the collaboration's own site still uses the future tense.
intervals.quote: CUPID will profit of the established CUORE cryogenic infrastructure, and deploy ~1500 Li2MoO4 crystals in place of the TeO2 ones.

quantity.quote: deploy ~1500 Li2MoO4 crystals in place of the TeO2 ones
The CUPID crystals will be grown from molybdenum enriched to ≥95 % in 100Mo and cut into 45×45×45 mm3 cubes, corresponding to a mass of ∼280 g per crystal, or a total 100Mo mass of 240 kg.

quantity.note: Given by the official site in comparison to CUORE's 130Te Q-value (2527 keV).
quantity.quote: a Q-value of 3034 keV (compared to 2527 keV of 130Te)

name: CUPID
notes: Located in LNGS in the existing CUORE cryostat, which the atlas places in Hall A (site:lngs-hall-a, via detector:cuore; that placement's source gives only the general LNGS location). The CUPID sources consulted state the general LNGS location, not the Hall A designation.

Status is recorded conservatively as 'proposed': the collaboration's site describes the detector only in the future tense and no primary source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives an unambiguous 'under construction' statement or a construction-start date. The March 2025 paper (arXiv:2503.02894) says construction activities 'have already started' (see the interval note). A secondary summary of a DOE CD-0 mission-need approval and a prototype under construction for mid-2025 data was not found in any primary source consulted.
No INSPIRE experiment-registry identifier is recorded for CUPID (external.inspire_experiment is empty).
No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives the collaboration's formation date.

physics_goals.quote: It will be hosted by the CUORE cryostat located at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso in Italy. The main physics goal of CUPID is to search for 0νββ of 100Mo ... CUPID aims at realizing a ton-scale experiment using Li2 MoO4 scintillating crystals isotopically enriched in 100Mo
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of 100Mo with a ton-scale array of scintillating bolometers, reusing the CUORE cryostat

summary.plain: The planned successor to CUORE: about 1500 crystals of a different material (lithium molybdate) that both glow and register heat, reusing CUORE's giant refrigerator under an Italian mountain to search for a rare radioactive process even more precisely.
summary.technical: CUPID (CUORE Upgrade with Particle IDentification): proposed ton-scale array of ~1500 Li2MoO4 scintillating bolometers targeting 0νββ of 100Mo (Qbb = 3034 keV), reusing the CUORE cryostat at LNGS. Successor to CUORE; no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a construction-start date.

unique_capabilities.quote: a scintillating material with a particle-dependent light yield
unique_capabilities.value: Scintillating bolometers (heat + light readout) give particle-type discrimination that CUORE's plain TeO2 bolometers lack, suppressing alpha backgrounds
